haiku-low.q1: After the Message Store write commits. The ack carries the message id (msgId) and the seq.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error, and nothing is stored, fanned out or received. The retry must carry the same clientMsgId.
haiku-low.q3: 30 seconds after its last heartbeat. Heartbeats are sent every 10 seconds, and the presence entry expires at 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: The worker treats the recipient as offline for that message: it writes an inbox entry and sends a push. After 5 seconds it also asks the gateway to close the session and clear presence.
haiku-low.q5: It is logged and ignored. Nothing is retried, and nothing stored is touched.
haiku-low.q6: In seq order within each conversation, drained from the inbox sorted by (conversation, seq). The client drops duplicates by msgId.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row, written in the same transaction as the message and seq. The relay publishes unsent rows after a restart, so a crash after commit does not lose the message.
haiku-low.q8: The Presence Store, which maps user to gateway node. The entry expires 30 seconds after the last heartbeat, which removes it.
haiku-low.q9: The worker sends a deliver request to the user's gateway node, which pushes it to the client. The client's ack goes to the gateway, which answers the worker within 5 seconds.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, per user, holding (conv, seq, msgId) references. It is written when the recipient is offline or does not ack within 5 seconds. An entry is deleted once the client acks it, or expires after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The user's Offline Inbox, read in (conversation, seq) order. Each body is then loaded from the Message Store and streamed.
haiku-low.q12: The queue message is not committed, so the queue redelivers it and the whole message is processed again. Recipients who already got it may get duplicates, which the client drops.

sonnet.q1: Only after the Message Store write (message, outbox row, seq) commits. The ack carries the message id and the seq.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error, nothing is stored or fanned out, and no one receives anything. The retry must carry the same client-generated message id (clientMsgId), so the unique key on (conversation, clientMsgId) prevents a second copy.
sonnet.q3: After 30 seconds with no heartbeat (heartbeats are every 10 s; the presence entry expires 30 s after the last heartbeat).
sonnet.q4: The recipient is treated as offline for that message: the worker writes an inbox entry (idempotent), asks that user's gateway node to close the session and clear presence, then sends a best-effort push and re-checks presence (sending a drain request if the user is now online). A late ack is ignored; the client drops any later duplicate.
sonnet.q5: It is logged and ignored. Nothing is retried and nothing stored is affected.
sonnet.q6: In seq order within each conversation (the drain reads the inbox sorted by (conversation, seq)). Duplicates are dropped by the client using message id.
sonnet.q7: The outbox row, written in the same Message Store transaction as the message. The relay polls rows with sent_at empty, so after a crash the unsent rows wait in the outbox and are published later.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Store (maps user to gateway node). The entry expires by TTL 30 seconds after the last heartbeat, which removes it when the connection dies uncleanly.
sonnet.q9: The worker looks up presence to find the user's gateway node and sends that node a deliver request. The gateway pushes the message over the WebSocket to the client. The client's ack goes to the gateway, which answers the worker's request (the worker waits up to 5 seconds).
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox (per recipient, holding references (conv, seq, msgId) only). It is written by the worker when the recipient is offline or does not ack within 5 s (idempotent on user, conversation, seq). An entry is deleted by the gateway once the client acks it during drain, or it expires after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: The gateway reads the user's Offline Inbox ordered by (conversation, seq), loads each body from the Message Store, and streams the entries. It re-reads the inbox until a read returns empty before registering presence. The client's last-seq is not used to skip entries; it is only for the history fallback.
sonnet.q12: The queue message is uncommitted until every recipient is acked or in the inbox, so the queue redelivers it and it is processed again. Recipients who already got it may receive it again, and the client drops the duplicate.
